**Two judgment calls worth your attention:**

1. **The Apple MacBook was capitalized, not expensed.** GBP 2,349 × 1.2500 (March policy rate) = USD 2,936.25, which clears the USD 2,500 threshold. Because depreciation starts the month *after* acquisition, there's **no March depreciation** on it — but **April UK depreciation should rise by GBP 65.25 to GBP 1,215.25**, and the fixed asset register needs asset UK-0231 added. Flagging so the April schedule doesn't get missed.
2. **Atlassian was fully expensed** — single-month coverage, so no prepaid treatment.

No entry exceeded the posting limit (largest was USD 2,936), so no approval requests were needed.

**What I couldn't clear — EXC-001, GBP 3,840.00:** the 2026-03-17 "FASTER PAYMENT OUT - REF 88213 KLM CONSULT." There is zero documentation for this anywhere — no invoice, contract, SOW or email — and KLM Consult isn't an existing UK vendor (your UK vendors are Kingsway, Albion, Camden, Octopus, Thistle). I searched by name, by reference 88213 and by amount; the bank statement line is the only trace.

I deliberately did **not** book it to 6520 Consulting Fees. The memo makes it tempting, but a bank narrative isn't support, and that would be posting purely to flatten the account. It stays in Suspense until AP/Treasury identifies the payee — at which point we also need to settle whether any of it is unearned at 3/31 and the VAT treatment.

Ending UK Suspense is **GBP 3,840.00, entirely this one item.** I left the checklist items open — this touches "Bank reconciliations," but that rec isn't finished and March depreciation still needs booking, so I didn't want to falsely signal completion.
